title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from the cote and the notation): k is a field of characteristic 0, and v, w : k -> C are two complex embeddings. xi_v^Z and xi_w^Z are the integral Betti realization (fibre) functors on motives over k. They send the motive of a smooth projective X/k to H^*((X ⊗_{k,v} C)^an, Z), respectively H^*((X ⊗_{k,w} C)^an, Z). The question is whether the two integral fibre functors are tensor-isomorphic. Rationally, or after Ẑ- or l-adic completion, comparison isomorphisms are standard. The integral question is genuinely subtle.

Claim 1: if k is countable (for example of finite type over Q), then xi_v^Z ≅ xi_w^Z.

Proof as written:
(i) Write k as a filtered union of a countable family of finitely generated subalgebras A_i.
(ii) After localizing, one may assume the transition maps Spec A_j -> Spec A_i are smooth with geometrically connected fibres.
(iii) Spread X out to smooth projective models X_i -> Spec A_i. Then the transition maps X_j -> X_i, and their complexifications X_{jC} -> X_{iC}, are also smooth with geometrically connected fibres.
(iv) The embeddings v and w give compatible complex points x_i, y_i of the bases (the page writes them in X_{iC}; the point is the same).
(v) Let pi^1(x_i, y_i) be the set of homotopy classes of paths from x_i to y_i. Connectedness of fibres makes the transition maps pi^1(x_j, y_j) -> pi^1(x_i, y_i) surjective.
(vi) A countable inverse system of nonempty sets with surjective transitions has nonempty limit (Mittag-Leffler). So lim pi^1(x_i, y_i) ≠ ∅.
(vii) A compatible system of paths gives, by parallel transport in the locally constant sheaves R^q f_* Z (Ehresmann), isomorphisms H^*(X_v, Z) ≅ H^*(X_w, Z). These are compatible with all algebraic correspondences and with tensor products, hence give a tensor isomorphism xi_v^Z ≅ xi_w^Z. The same choice of path works for all objects at once, because everything is spread out over the same base.

Claim 2 (begun): if k is not countable, Grothendieck asserts there is a counterexample. Part 2) starts to build it: there should exist an index alpha such that xi_v^Z and xi_w^Z are not isomorphic when restricted to M_alpha(X), apparently a subcategory of motives attached to X or to a family over X. He then says one may reduce to X = Spec K with K a number field. The rest is crossed out and left unfinished.

What the page serves: whether the 'Galois group' of motives with Z coefficients is attached to a well-defined torsor class independent of the embedding. Over countable fields the integral Betti torsor is trivial between different embeddings; over uncountable fields it need not be.
errors: Step (ii), arranging all transition maps Spec A_j -> Spec A_i to be smooth with geometrically connected fibres, needs justification. Generically the extensions are of finite type and the A_i can be shrunk, but making this compatible along the whole system requires care. Geometric connectedness of fibres is plausible because k is the union of the A_i and the fraction fields are subfields of k, but this is not argued.
Points x_i, y_i should lie in (Spec A_i)(C), not in X_{iC}; path transport happens on the base. This is likely just a notational slip.

For the inverse limit to be nonempty one needs a countable cofinal subsystem. Hence 'dénombrable' replaced the crossed-out 'suite de générateurs'. This is correct, but the countable index set should be made explicit.

The uncountable counterexample is only announced, not given. The reduction to X = Spec K is unclear: for Artin motives the comparison torsor is a limit of finite nonempty sets and hence nonempty by compactness, so the obstruction must come from elsewhere.

ideas.what: Integral Betti fibre functors for two complex embeddings of a countable field are tensor-isomorphic. Proof: spread out over finitely generated bases and choose a compatible system of paths, using Mittag-Leffler for path torsors under surjective transitions.
ideas.modern_name: Integral comparison of Betti realizations of conjugate varieties; trivialisation of the integral Betti-Betti torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore around conjugate varieties (Serre 1964 on non-homeomorphic conjugates; Deligne's torsor of comparison isomorphisms in Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, 1982, rational/adelic version)
ideas.where_published: unsure; not in EGA/SGA as far as known

ideas.what: Surjectivity of pi_1 / path torsors along smooth morphisms with connected fibres, and nonemptiness of a countable inverse limit of nonempty sets with surjective transitions
ideas.modern_name: Mittag-Leffler argument; homotopy exact sequence for fibrations

ideas.what: Assertion that for uncountable k (e.g. k = C with wild automorphisms) the integral Betti fibre functors attached to different embeddings may fail to be isomorphic
ideas.modern_name: Non-triviality of the integral comparison torsor for conjugate varieties over uncountable fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (related to Serre's conjugate varieties example)

missed.claim: Over an uncountable field, the integral Betti realizations for two embeddings v, w need not be tensor-isomorphic, even restricted to a single 'M_alpha(X)'. The counterexample construction begins but is abandoned. The dichotomy countable/uncountable for integral fibre functors on motives is a sharp statement.
missed.quote: Si k pas dénombrable, on a un contre-exemple ... il existe α tel que ξ_v^Z | M_α(X) ≄ ξ_w^Z | M_α(X)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral structures on motivic Galois groups and on Betti-to-Betti torsors (e.g. for conjugate varieties, integral period torsors) are studied today. A clean set-theoretic cardinality obstruction to integral comparison would be a notable precise statement. I am not aware of it being stated in this form.

missed.claim: Complete short proof that, for countable k, the integral Betti fibre functors for any two complex embeddings are tensor-isomorphic. The proof uses spreading out plus a countable Mittag-Leffler choice of compatible paths.
missed.quote: les morphismes de transition π^1(x_j,y_j) → π^1(x_i,y_i) sont surjectifs. Donc lim π^1(x_i,y_i) ≠ ∅, cqfd.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives an explicit integral comparison that the usual literature only treats rationally or adelically; it is relevant to integral motivic Galois group questions. It is probably folklore among experts, so novelty is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: A tidy and correct argument for integral comparison of Betti functors over countable fields, plus an announced but unwritten uncountable counterexample. Both are plausible folklore but not standardly recorded in this form. The counterexample itself is missing from the page.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 insertion reads 'dénombrable (p.ex. de type fini sur Q)', which replaces the crossed-out 'une suite de générateurs'.
'pts x_i, y_i dans X_{iC}' — the image indeed shows X_i C; mathematically these are points of (Spec A_i)(C).
The inserted line before 2) appears to read '(on a un contre-exemple ...) E' only tentatively; the handwriting is uncertain.
